What this page is. A visual companion to the full lab (DIG123_Lab03_Module5_Sprint1-Kit-User-Story-Set_FULL.md). Every step has a short animation of a mock-up6, what you do, and when you are done. The example team, Team Menu, is fictional; write your own product and your own words. Module 4 had no lab, so this is Lab 03; it merges the old D4 (Deliverable 4, Sprint 1 Kit) and D5 (Deliverable 5, User Story Set & forecast) bricks. Today's PO (Product Owner) (Product Owner) is member 2 and the SM (Scrum Master) (Scrum Master) is member 3.
1 h lecture (input)
2 h Team Studio
1 h Home Sprint

1 · 2 · 1 — your lab work is 3 hours at most; the lecture hour, the reading and the Learning Log are not counted.

Tools are open. Every tool named on this page is a starting point, never a rule. Use any other suitable and available tool — or create your own (a spreadsheet that draws the burndown, a small script that computes the forecast). Be creative and research thoroughly before you adopt a tool: official site only, free-tier limits, licence and terms (Legal Notice §6.6, §14), a link check with VirusTotal and Google Safe Browsing (Annex C), and five minutes of trying it as a team. This is not a cybersecurity course; the check takes two minutes.

Part A · Team Studio (120 minutes, in class)

0

Planning

⏱ 10 min

The Facilitator reads the D2 vision sentence and the Sprint 1 Goal from Class 4. The Scribe writes today's goal. Hats are given out. The PO (PO (Product Owner), member 2 today) reads the <strong>top eight</strong> backlog items aloud, in order. The rest stay on a <strong>later list</strong>.

Done when: The goal is on the page, everyone knows their hat, and the eight items are in front of the team.

Backlog on a wall, a sheet or a board<sup><a class="fnref" href="#fn2" id="r2">2</a></sup> — your choice.

1a

Write eight user stories

⏱ 12 min

Each member takes two items and writes them alone, in silence: <strong>As a</strong> [a user of your D2] <strong>I want</strong> [one action, no technique] <strong>so that</strong> [the benefit the user feels]. The Scribe types all eight into Box 1.

Done when: Eight stories, each with a real D2 user, an action without technique and a benefit that does not repeat the action.
1b

Test every story with INVEST (Independent, Negotiable, Valuable, Estimable, Small, Testable)

⏱ 13 min

Answer the six questions for every story and mark each letter ✓ or ✗. Rewrite until <strong>at most one ✗</strong> remains and write one line for each ✗ you keep. Too big? Split by user, by step of the journey or by rule — and keep the total at eight.

Done when: An INVEST row for every story with at most one ✗, each explained.
1c

One acceptance test per story

⏱ 10 min

One line: <strong>Given</strong> the starting situation, <strong>when</strong> one action, <strong>then</strong> one result that can be <em>observed</em> — with a number where possible. A member who did not write the story reads it aloud and answers “yes, I can see that” or “no, I cannot”. Then the PO states the final order (5 min).

Done when: Eight tests that a second person could check, and an order the PO has said aloud.
2

Definition of Done: five checks

⏱ 10 min

Start from the Class 4 checks. Test each with four questions: a yes-or-no question? Can someone other than the author answer it? In ten minutes or less? The same for every story? Keep exactly five, numbered, and write the rule sentence.

Done when: Five numbered yes-or-no checks and the rule: all five yes, or the story is not Done.
3a

Planning Poker with fingers

⏱ 12 min

Smallest story = 1 point. Count “one, two, three” and everybody shows 1, 2 or 3 fingers, an open hand (5) or a fist (8) at the same moment; a flat hand means “cannot estimate yet”. If the numbers differ by more than one step, the highest and the lowest explain for 30 seconds and the team votes again (two re-votes at most; then take the higher).

Done when: Every story has points; each disagreement has a one-word note.

Fingers need no tool; online versions exist<sup><a class="fnref" href="#fn4" id="r4">4</a></sup> — read their terms first.

3b

MoSCoW (Must have, Should have, Could have, Won't have this time) letters

⏱ 8 min

The PO proposes a letter for each story with the test questions; the Developers may challenge. Check: Must points are at most about 60 % of the total, and every Won't has a one-line reason. Write the totals per letter.

Done when: Every story has a letter; the totals are written; each Won't has a reason.
4

Sprint Goal, content and forecast

⏱ 15 min

<strong>4a (5 min)</strong> Sprint Goal: one sentence, an outcome for a user, judged “met / not met” by looking at one thing. <strong>4b (3 min)</strong> List the Sprint 1 stories and add their points: the total of your burndown and your planned velocity. <strong>4c (7 min)</strong> Remaining = Must + Should points − Sprint 1 points; Sprints = remaining ÷ velocity, <strong>rounded up</strong>; do it again with velocity × 0.7. Sprints end on Oct 25, Nov 8, Nov 22, Dec 6 and Dec 20.

Done when: A Sprint Goal that passes the three tests, a burndown total, two forecasts with end dates, and one sentence on what would make the cautious case happen.
R

Sprint Review, Retrospective, plan the week

⏱ 25 min

<strong>Review (15 min):</strong> the Presenter shows story 1 — sentence, test, points, letter — and the Sprint Goal in 90 seconds; the class asks one INVEST question. <strong>Retrospective (5 min):</strong> start / stop / continue, one note per person per column. <strong>Step 5 (5 min):</strong> write who does the Daily Scrums, who updates the burndown, when the Sprint 1 Review happens, and who exports the PDF.

Done when: The question and answer are in the footer; three retro notes; four names for the week.

Part B · Home Sprint (60 minutes, spread over the week)

6

Three Daily Scrum lines

⏱ 10 min

Choose three real Daily Scrums from Sprint 1 on three different days. Each line has four parts: <strong>date · progress toward the Sprint Goal (points Done of the total) · impediment · what we change in the plan</strong>. Example: <em>Sat Oct 17 · 1 of 9 · none · behind the ideal line, so icons wait until French is Done.</em>

Done when: Three real lines with four parts each; the plan changed when the team was behind.
7

The Sprint 1 burndown

⏱ 15 min

Day 1 = Mon Oct 12 … day 14 = Sun Oct 25. Ideal at the end of day <em>d</em> = total × (14 − <em>d</em>) ÷ 14. Actual = total − points of stories that pass <strong>all five</strong> checks. Draw both lines with any tool<sup><a class="fnref" href="#fn1" id="r1">1</a></sup><sup><a class="fnref" href="#fn3" id="r3">3</a></sup>, label the axes, and write two sentences on what the shape tells you.

Done when: The ideal line starts at the Sprint 1 total and reaches 0 on day 14; the reading is written.
8

Sprint 1 Review and Retrospective: five lines

⏱ 15 min

Hold both events at the end of the Sprint (online is fine; one real user or stakeholder if you can). Write five lines: goal met? · real velocity and the updated forecast · what the user said · one change for Sprint 2 (owner, date) and one shortcut to repay · one thing to keep.

Done when: Five lines, with the real velocity and the updated forecast.
9

The “done when” checks + one cold read

⏱ 10 min

Five checks: eight stories pass INVEST and every test is observable · five numbered Done checks · the numbers add up · three real Daily Scrum lines · five Review lines. Then one member reads the whole page cold and marks where they stumbled. Fix those places; do not start a new debate.

Done when: All five checks are true and the cold-read marks are fixed.
10

Export, name, submit

⏱ 10 min

One PDF named <code>DIG123_D4D5_&lt;TeamName&gt;_2026-10-25.pdf</code>. <strong>Each member</strong> submits it on Blackboard → DIG 123 → Assignments and adds their own Learning Log (five lines). Move your board card to Done and create the card for Lab 04.

Done when: Every member has submitted the PDF and a Learning Log.

Notes on tools and versions (checked October 2026)

  1. Spreadsheet and chart menus differ between Google Sheets, LibreOffice Calc and Excel, and they change with each version. The path to a line chart may be named differently from what you have seen; search the tool's own help for “line chart”. Official sites: Google Sheets, LibreOffice. ↩
  2. Boards change their free tiers, limits and screens often: Trello, GitHub Projects, Jira, Focalboard, Wekan, Taiga. Read the current limits and terms on the official site before you adopt one. ↩
  3. Mermaid chart blocks change between versions; read the syntax for the version you use in its documentation at mermaid.js.org. A spreadsheet or graph paper works just as well. ↩
  4. Online Planning Poker sites appear, change and disappear; their terms and data handling differ. Check the site first with the link checks of Annex C of the Legal Notice. The technique is described by Mountain Goat Software. ↩
  5. As of October 2026 the Scrum Guide 2020 is the current edition on scrumguides.org. It does not prescribe user stories, story points, velocity or burndown charts; they are common practices used in this course. ↩
  6. The animations on this page are schematic mock-ups drawn for this lab, not screenshots of any product. Real tools look different and may have changed since October 2026.
